key_insight: At the initial physician evaluation, Dr. CaBot and pediatric emergency physicians both produced high-scoring differential diagnoses in 95% of cases.
clinical_relevance: Agentic AI may offer diagnostic support in pediatric emergency care, but improved patient outcomes have not been demonstrated.
method: Retrospective study of 100 randomly selected, age-stratified pediatric emergency encounters resulting in admission or surgery.
Compared Dr. CaBot with and without literature search against four attending pediatric emergency physicians across four documentation touchpoints.
Two independent physician reviewers established ground truth and scored differentials while masked to their source.
evidence_signal: At the prespecified primary touchpoint, the difference in high-scoring differentials was 0 percentage points (95% CI: −5.8 to 5.8); no differences were detected at other touchpoints.
watch_item: This single-center retrospective documentation study requires prospective validation before conclusions about real-world safety or benefit.
paper_title: Agentic AI versus pediatric emergency physicians for differential diagnosis of acutely ill and injured children
